observe_how: The comment at line 223 claims storage happens 'only on actual error patterns (TypeError, ENOENT, etc.)' but ERROR_PATTERNS leads with bare /\berror\b/i, /\bfailed\b/i, /\bfailure\b/i, /\btimeout\b/i — words present in most healthy agent reports ('all tests passed, 0 errors', 'added error handling'). The G3 quality scorer drops NOISE (<3) but BORDERLINE (3-4) passes, so plausible-looking false failures land tagged agent_failure/FAILED_APPROACH. Query archival_memory for tags LIKE '%agent_failure%' and sample: entries quoting success summaries confirm. Separately, the store is execSync with a 10s ceiling inside PostToolUse:Agent — every false positive adds seconds of blocking latency after agent completion (cf. SEED-16's same store-hot-path pattern). Fix: drop the bare error/failed/failure/timeout words (keep stack-trace and errno patterns), and use detached spawn like post-plan-roadmap does.
telemetry: memory-recall hit-rate 27.4%; every Task completion whose text contains 'error' pays the scorer + possible 10s execSync

title: agent-verification delivers its entire output (the verification warning) via the legacy top-level 'message' field that the repo's own types/docs mark deprecated — warnings likely never reach Claude, making the hook decorative

evidence.quote: - Context injection: `PostToolUse additionalContext` is the reliable inject pattern

observe_how: The hook's sole purpose is injecting '⚠️ AGENT VERIFICATION WARNING' context after suspicious agent claims, but it never uses hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext — only { message }, which shared/types.ts labels legacy/deprecated and hook-dev-lifecycle.md contrasts with the 'reliable inject pattern'. Sibling hooks on the same event (ralph-task-monitor, post-plan-roadmap) all wrap context in hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. Secondary nit: the existsSync check at lines 146-151 tests bare filenames ('!file.includes("/")') relative to the hook process cwd, generating false 'files that don't exist' warnings for valid relative paths — low-stakes only because the channel is dead. Observe: trigger a kraken/spark response claiming completion without files and check that no warning appears in context. Fix: route warnings through additionalContext (one-function change).
telemetry: Registered on PostToolUse matcher=Agent; warning deliveries observable in transcripts: none expected via legacy field

title: architecture-stats-sync: non-unref'd 1s safety-net setTimeout in readStdin keeps the hook process alive ~1 second on EVERY Bash PostToolUse — a fixed latency floor added to every Bash call in the session
observe_how: The timer is never cleared or unref'd, so even after stdin 'end' resolves and main() prints its output, the live timer holds the event loop and the process cannot exit until ~1000ms have elapsed. Claude Code waits for hook exit, so every Bash tool call registered to this hook pays ~1s. One-line fix: `setTimeout(...).unref()` or clearTimeout on 'end'.
telemetry: wall-time of the architecture-stats-sync hook per Bash call (should be ~50ms Node startup, observed ~1s+)

title: architecture-stats-sync: fires off HEAD without checking the commit command actually succeeded — a FAILED `git commit` (hook denial, nothing staged) still inspects the PREVIOUS commit and can spuriously launch the background sync
observe_how: Payoff: gate on detectToolError(input.tool_response) (already exists in shared/tool-error.ts) so a failed commit whose HEAD happens to touch .claude/hooks doesn't re-run the stats sync; sync is idempotent so impact is wasted work, not corruption.
telemetry: .claude/logs/architecture-stats-sync.log entries with no corresponding new commit
